topic: Error Propagation in Addition, Subtraction, Multiplication and Division
title: Errors Grow: Error Propagation Explained Simply | PUC Physics Class 11
description:
A tailor, a builder and a painter all combine measured lengths, and every length hides a small error. Aarav's study table is 120 cm by 60 cm, each side good to 1 mm. Is the area off by 1 square millimetre? No: by 18 square centimetres. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Physics (Chapter 1, Units and Measurement) we see how errors travel into a result.

On a live measuring bench we add and subtract two rods and watch the worst-case error bar grow, then stretch the table top and see the two thin strips that make the area error. We derive both rules step by step: for Z = A + B or A - B the absolute errors add, and for Z = AB or A/B the relative (percentage) errors add. Two pause-and-think questions, a fully worked example, the exam trap about subtracting errors, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, JEE Main and NEET students.
